options.title: ไดโนน้อยตามหาไข่วันเกิด
options.pitch: ผจญภัยเป็นเพื่อนไดโนเสาร์น้อย ตามหาไข่หายในห้องนั่งเล่นแล้วนำไปฉลองที่เค้กยักษ์ ทุกคนจบเกมได้ในรอบสั้น ๆ และได้เสียงเชียร์จากโซฟา
options.core_loop: เดินตามรอยไข่ไดโนเสาร์ แตะจุดหมายเพื่อเก็บไข่ทีละฟอง แล้วกลับมาฉลองที่เค้ก

options.title: สนามไดโนเสาร์ไขลาน
options.pitch: ห้องนั่งเล่นกลายเป็นสนามของเล่นไดโนเสาร์ เด็กถือดาบของเล่น ตีไดโนเสาร์ไขลานให้กลิ้งกลับไป และเผชิญหน้าเจ้าตัวใหญ่ยิ้มแย้มในฉากจบ
options.core_loop: ยืนตรงกลาง ฟันดาบของเล่นใส่ไดโนเสาร์ของเล่นที่เดินเข้ามา และก้าวออกจากวงแหวนเตือน

options.title: หมากนักขุดฟอสซิล
options.pitch: กลายเป็นหมากนักสำรวจตัวจิ๋ว เดินไต่กระดานขุดฟอสซิล หลบไดโนเสาร์ยามของเล่น และประกอบโครงกระดูกให้สมบูรณ์
options.core_loop: เดินเหมือนตัวหมากบนแผนที่ฟอสซิล เลือกช่องปลอดภัยเพื่อเก็บฟอสซิลตามลำดับ

on.recommend_why: แนะนำ “ไดโนน้อยตามหาไข่วันเกิด” เพราะเด็กมือใหม่เดินช้า ๆ แล้วจบได้ในห้องเล็กอย่างปลอดภัย ทั้งยังให้ความค้นพบ ความน่ารัก และช่วงฉลองร่วมกับผู้ชมครบที่สุดค่ะ

prototype.title: ไดโนน้อยตามหาไข่วันเกิด
prototype.logline: คุณคือเพื่อนไดโนเสาร์น้อย เดินตามรอยเท้าเพื่อหาไข่ที่หายไป ช่วยนำไข่กลับรัง แล้วเข้าประตูเค้กยักษ์ให้ทุกคนบนโซฟาร่วมฉลอง
pillars: ค้นหาง่ายด้วยภาพใหญ่และทีละขั้น

storyboard.title: ตามรอยเท้า
storyboard.caption: รอยเท้าสีสดโผล่บนพื้นห้องจริง และไดโนเสาร์น้อยตัวกลมยืนรออย่างเป็นมิตร
storyboard.player_does: ยืนที่จุดเริ่มกับผู้ใหญ่ แล้วเดินช้า ๆ ตามรอยเท้าไปแตะจุดหมายแรก

storyboard.title: เจอไข่และเพื่อนตัวน้อย
storyboard.caption: พบไข่สีเขียวลายจุด จากนั้นมีแอ่งโคลนสีแดงนุ่มนวลกั้นทางแคบ ๆ ก่อนถึงเพื่อนไดโนเสาร์
storyboard.player_does: แตะเก็บไข่ มองวงแดงแล้วเดินอ้อม จากนั้นไปแตะจุดช่วยไดโนเสาร์น้อย

storyboard.title: นำไข่กลับรัง
storyboard.caption: รังใบใหญ่และไดโนเสาร์ครอบครัวปรากฏข้างทางเดิน พร้อมเค้กวันเกิดที่มองเห็นจากโซฟา
storyboard.player_does: เดินไปแตะจุดหมายสุดท้ายเพื่อนำไข่เข้ารัง โดยไม่ต้องรีบหรือมองขึ้น

storyboard.title: ฉลองที่เค้กยักษ์
storyboard.caption: ประตูเค้กเปิดหันเข้าหาโซฟา ไดโนเสาร์ยืนอยู่ข้างฉากจบให้ทุกคนเห็นผู้เล่นเดินเข้าประตู
storyboard.player_does: เดินเข้าประตูเค้ก รับคำยินดีและเสียงเชียร์ แล้วให้ผู้ใหญ่ช่วยถอดแว่นเพื่อผลัดคนต่อไป

decisions.what: ธีมและโอกาสของเกม

decisions.what: รูปแบบการเล่นและเวลา
decisions.choice: เล่นคนเดียวผลัดกัน รอบละประมาณ 3 นาที ไม่จับเวลาและไม่จัดอันดับ

decisions.what: เส้นทางและจุดหมาย
decisions.choice: วงเดินสั้น 4 จุดเรียงลำดับ ได้แก่ ตามรอยเท้า เจอไข่สีเขียว ช่วยไดโนเสาร์น้อย นำไข่ไปที่รัง แล้วเข้าประตูเค้ก

decisions.what: ระดับความน่ากลัว
decisions.choice: ไม่มีฉากไล่ล่า เสียงตกใจ แสงสยอง หรือพื้นหลุม ไดโนเสาร์ทุกตัวยิ้มและอยู่ข้างทาง
decisions.quote: ห้ามน่ากลัว

decisions.what: สีของฉากและอุปสรรค
decisions.choice: ใช้ชุดสีของเล่นน้ำเงิน เหลือง เขียว และครีม โดยเก็บสีแดงไว้เฉพาะแอ่งโคลนเพื่อให้เด็กแยกอันตรายได้ทันที

decisions.what: การจัดวางไดโนเสาร์
decisions.choice: วางโมเดลไดโนเสาร์ข้างเส้นทางเป็นฉากให้ค้นพบ ไม่วางบนทางเดินและไม่ให้ไล่ผู้เล่น

decisions.what: ช่วงฉลองและผู้ชม
decisions.choice: ประตูเค้กหันเข้าหาโซฟา ฉลองทุกคนที่จบโดยไม่เปรียบเทียบคะแนนหรืออันดับ

decisions.what: การช่วยเหลือผู้เล่นอายุน้อย
decisions.choice: มีผู้ใหญ่ช่วยใส่แว่น ปรับสาย และเดินอยู่ใกล้ตลอดรอบ เพราะผู้เล่นอายุต่ำกว่าช่วงที่ Meta แนะนำสำหรับ Quest

decisions.what: ผลของการเหยียบแอ่งโคลน
decisions.choice: หัก 25 คะแนนและส่งกลับจุดหมายล่าสุด โดยยังเล่นต่อและจบเกมได้ ไม่มีการแพ้

decisions.what: คะแนนเมื่อเล่นจบ
decisions.choice: จุดหมายแต่ละจุดให้ 100 คะแนน การเข้าประตูให้ 300 คะแนนและโบนัสเวลา แต่ HUD เน้นรางวัลไม่เน้นการแข่งขัน

build.name: ไดโนน้อยตามหาไข่วันเกิด
build.description: เดินตามรอยเท้า ตามหาไข่ไดโนเสาร์น้อยแล้วนำกลับรัง ก่อนฉลองวันเกิดที่ประตูเค้กยักษ์
build.goal: เดินแตะจุดหมายทั้ง 4 จุดตามลำดับ นำไข่กลับรัง แล้วเข้าประตูเค้กวันเกิด
rules: เล่นทีละ 1 คน โดยมีผู้ใหญ่ช่วยใส่แว่นและอยู่ใกล้ตลอดรอบ
เดินช้า ๆ ตามรอยเท้า และแตะจุดหมายให้ครบ 4 จุดตามลำดับ
อย่าเหยียบแอ่งโคลนสีแดง ถ้าเหยียบจะเสีย 25 คะแนนและกลับไปจุดหมายล่าสุด แต่เล่นต่อได้
เมื่อนำไข่ไปที่รังแล้ว ให้เดินเข้าประตูเค้กเพื่อจบเกมและรับเสียงเชียร์
ไม่มีเวลาจับและไม่จัดอันดับ ทุกคนที่เล่นจบได้รับการฉลอง

options.title: ดาบฟองสบู่กับไดโนลูกโป่ง

options.core_loop: ฟองดาบฟองสบู่ใส่ไดโนเสาร์ลูกโป่งและก้าวออกจากวงเตือนก่อนหยดน้ำตกลงมา

options.title: กระดานของขวัญไดโนตัวจิ๋ว
options.pitch: กลายเป็นหมากไดโนเสาร์บนกระดานปาร์ตี้ยักษ์ เดินทีละช่องเพื่อหาทางเก็บของขวัญโดยไม่ชนไดโนเสาร์ของเล่นที่เดินเป็นจังหวะ
options.core_loop: ดูช่องที่ไดโนเสาร์ของเล่นจะเดินไป แล้วเดินตามช่องปลอดภัยไปเก็บของขวัญตามลำดับ

judge.reason_on: fit 8: 4 checkpoints, one hazard, no timer and no ranking suit eight 5-6 year olds taking turns in a 3 x 3.5 m room, and the cake portal faces the sofa. buildable 9: everything is checkpoints, one red hazard, a portal and static smiling dino vignettes, and the counts match across option, prototype and layout. safe_mr 8: there is an adult escort, the under-10 Meta age guidance is noted, red is kept only for the hazard and the dinos are never on the path; the portal is quite close to the sofa where children sit. specific 8: exact Thai labels, hex palette, hazard placed between checkpoints 2 and 3, and a timed flow. correct 8: clean Thai and a correct age note; 'no clock' sits a little oddly beside the engine's time bonus.
judge.reason_off: fit 8: the egg-hatching birthday party theme is on brief, and the round is untimed at about 3 min. buildable 6: it invents event mechanics (eggs hatch at checkpoint 4, a baby dino 'pops up' at each point, a footprint arrow appears when the child stops looking); the layout puts mud 2 between checkpoints 3 and 4 but the sketch puts it elsewhere; and 'start' is listed as a checkpoint label but is missing from the sketch zones. safe_mr 7: 5 checkpoints plus 2 hazards is a lot for a tiny room with a 1.2 m lane, though it does suggest a PC version for children. specific 7: pastel palette and clear labels. correct 6: the mud is brown in the palette and key art but a red circle in the layout, which is contradictory and also clashes with the engine's red hazards.

judge.why: X is sized to the tiny living room with one gentle hazard and a finish that faces the sofa; Y crams 5 stops and 2 hazards into the same space and relies on a hatching event the engine can't trigger.
judge.reason_on: fit 8: cute dino egg hunt, cake portal facing sofa, no timer or ranking, adult help, Meta age note. buildable 8: 4 checkpoints + 1 hazard fits the under-4x4 rule; everything is static scenery. safe_mr 7: single soft hazard with bypass, dinos off path; but calls the hazard segment 'narrow' and softens edge margin to 'where possible'. specific 8: labels, hex palette with red reserved for hazard, portal on sofa side matches sketch. correct 8: clean Thai. overall 8.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: pastel party, hatching surprise, singing on finish; sofa shown in a corner away from the finish. buildable 5: eggs hatching in front of the mother is a triggered event the engine lacks; 5 checkpoints + 2 hazards claimed with 1.2 m corridor and 0.6 m margins in 3 x 3.5 m (about 1.8 x 2.3 m usable) does not fit. safe_mr 5: cramped loop with two rings for first-time 5-year-olds. specific 7: rich palette, but mud is brown in palette/key art while hazards are red circles. correct 7: 'ใส่ชุด' for putting on a headset is odd wording. overall 5.

judge.why: Y actually writes down accurate, player-facing science and uses only label-based mechanics. X's hidden-clue idea cannot be built and leaves the accuracy constraint unaddressed.
judge.reason_on: fit 9: every checkpoint label carries a short fact, the asteroid belt sits between Mars and Jupiter as the climax, the not-to-scale note is on the intro card, and a pre/post ordering test serves the lesson. buildable 8: exact labels, coordinates and 2 hazards; the 'hologram arrows' are decor and the Neptune/portal coordinates differ slightly between sketch and layout. safe_mr 8: 1.5-3 m spacing, 1.2 m lanes, a non-void floor, and the finish is at the bleachers. specific 9: normalized coordinates for every planet, palette, and timed flow. correct 8: all 8 facts are right (Venus hottest, Uranus axial tilt, liquid water on Earth); there is a typo 'ลำบับ' in the pitch, and 'night' lighting in a sunny morning gym is questionable.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: 8 planets in correct order, 4 players on a shared floor, a 240 s limit and a disclaimer that the layout is not to scale. buildable 6: it relies on a 'clue for the next planet without naming it' system that the engine does not have, since a checkpoint only has its label and the labels are the planet names, so the HUD would give the answer away; the number of hazards is left vague. safe_mr 8: 1.2 m lanes, static gaps, and the dodge is placed toward the bleachers. specific 6: the sketch lumps Mercury to Mars into one zone and no clue text is written. correct 6: 'data must be accurate' is the key constraint, yet none of the facts players will read are actually given, so they cannot be checked.

judge.why: Y puts correct, kid-readable facts into the labels the engine actually shows and gives exact coordinates; X's riddle mechanic depends on clue text the runner has no slot for.
judge.reason_on: fit 8: walking the order plus one fact per planet directly teaches; finish by bleachers. buildable 7: facts live in the checkpoint labels themselves (engine-native); 2 hazard patches; minor sketch vs build-plan mismatch on Neptune/portal coordinates. safe_mr 7: 2 hazards only, 1.5-3 m spacing, no void; 'night' lighting with window daylight may wash out. specific 9: exact labels, normalized coordinates, Jupiter biggest, Saturn rings prominent. correct 8: all 8 facts correct (Venus hottest, Earth surface liquid water, Uranus tilt); 'ลำบับ' typo only in creator-facing pitch. overall 8.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: 8 planets in order, shared floor for 4, asteroid belt at Mars-Jupiter, but hidden-name riddles plus a 4-min timer are heavy for first-time P.5. buildable 5: core mechanic is a clue for the next planet on each checkpoint, but checkpoints only carry a short label (here the planet name), so the clue layer has nowhere to live. safe_mr 7: few static rings, 1.2 m lanes for 4; spiral from centre crowds early. specific 7: palette and spiral, but sketch lumps 4 planets into one zone. correct 8: asteroid belt placement right, explicit not-to-scale disclaimer. overall 6.

judge.why: Y is safer and more buildable for a tiny mall floor; its misspelling is a quick fix. X's 4-hazard slalom and spawn/portal overlap are design problems.
judge.reason_on: fit 7: 120 s solo with a leaderboard, an original mascot and no ads; studio lighting suits the mall. The player-read title 'วิ่งไม่ได้ก็สนุกได้' ('you can't run but it's still fun') is an odd, negative pitch. buildable 6: the river 'gets more colourful as stops awaken' is a state change the engine lacks; the sketch puts the portal (0.28, 0.75) almost on top of spawn (0.24, 0.76). safe_mr 6: 4 hazards including a slalom inside a 4 x 4 m floor with a 1.2 m lane and 0.6 m margins is crowded for all ages and first-timers. specific 8: exact labels, hazard placement per segment and 18-24 props. correct 7: no errors, apart from the awkward title.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: 2 min solo, a leaderboard on the booth screen, no branding, and the finish faces the queue on the east side. buildable 7: mostly engine-native; the leaves that 'sprout' at checkpoints and the gate that 'lights up' are small invented reveals. safe_mr 8: only 2 hazard zones, a 'walk only' rule and generous gaps, which suits a 4 x 4 m floor; spawn is very close to checkpoint 1. specific 8: hex per element, compass layout. correct 5: 'ลำธาน' is misspelt (should be ลำธาร) in a player-facing checkpoint label and the story, and 'rotten fruit' hazards are an off-key choice for a juice brand's booth.

judge.why: Y is a bit safer on the tiny floor but ships a misspelled checkpoint label players will read and a rotten-fruit motif at a juice booth; X is more specific and on-brand, though it should drop a hazard and the river-colour promise.
judge.reason_on: fit 7: 120 s solo, leaderboard, no ads/logos, finish faces queue; studio lighting suits a bright mall. buildable 6: 'river becomes more colourful as stops wake' is a state change the engine can't do; 4 hazards + 5 checkpoints in 4 x 4 m is at the edge of the size rule. safe_mr 6: 0.6 m margins leave ~2.8 m inner square, a 4-ring slalom there squeezes the 1.2 m lane for mixed ages; Meta age note is good. specific 8: hazard-by-segment placement, 18-24 props, timed flow beats. correct 6: odd meta title 'วิ่งไม่ได้ก็สนุกได้:' reads awkwardly to players. overall 6.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: same core, no branding, queue-facing finish; 'morning' lighting is a less natural fit for an indoor mall. buildable 7: plain checkpoints, 2 hazard zones, nothing invented. safe_mr 7: fewer hazards keep the tiny floor walkable, though a 'ring cluster' with 1.2 m around it is optimistic. specific 7: hex palette by role, but spawn is south while queue/screen is east, so placement is inconsistent. correct 4: 'ลำธาน' (should be ลำธาร) is misspelled in a checkpoint label and the story; 'rotten fruit' hazards are an odd message at a juice brand booth. overall 5.

judge.why: Y's best hook, the tightening guard beat, is outside the tactics engine (guards must move every 3 s or slower). X stays within the rules and is consistent from start to end.
judge.reason_on: fit: the speedrun, total timer and clean-run leaderboard suit stream viewers and expression well. buildable: config beats of 2.5 s (rook) and 1.5 s (queen), and the '1.5-2 s' promise, break the engine rule that guards move every 3 s or slower; the option text says the knight has 2 'slow guards', yet the rook board's cracks and tables are unbalanced against the copy. safe/comfort: the fast final beat risks repeated failure, a risk Y names itself. specific: strong piece characterisation (spectral rider, castle golem) and a 6-colour palette. correct: the storyboard title ' halls of the Court' has a stray leading space and a lowercase start. overall: needs its beats fixed before build.
judge.reason_off: fit: knight-bishop-rook-queen ramp over four 6x8 boards fits a hard 10-min solo puzzle, and the stream can read the whole board; no leaderboard, though 'expression' could use one. buildable: every beat is 3.0-3.5 s, within the 3 s minimum, and targets/guards/tables/cracks rise steadily (2/1/0/0 up to 5/4/3/3), consistent with the prototype. safe/comfort: no countdown, restart-board control, readable threatened squares. specific: clear counts and palette, but zone and route notes stay generic. correct: clean English, no errors. overall: a solid, legal design.

judge.why: Y's difficulty rests on guard beats the tactics engine cannot run. X delivers the same concept entirely within the rules, with consistent counts.
judge.reason_on: fit 8: a harder curve, a clean-run speedrun leaderboard that suits streaming, and good piece characterisation. buildable 4: guard beats of 2.5 s and 1.5 s break the engine's 'every 3 s or slower' rule, and the mechanics and test questions build the climax on that faster beat. safe_mr 6: a 1.5 s beat with overlapping attacks hurts readability, the very thing its pillar promises. specific 8: detailed config and HUD. correct 6: the storyboard title ' halls of the Court' has a stray space and lowercase. overall 6.
judge.reason_off: fit 8: four 6x8 boards (knight, bishop, rook, queen) with ordered captures, a stream-readable whole-board camera and restart without countdown. The early boards (2 targets, 1 guard) are mild for a 'hard' brief. buildable 9: beats of 3.5/3.5/3.2/3.0 s respect the 3 s minimum, and the target, guard and obstacle counts match across mechanics, flow and config. safe_mr 8: clarity is the focus, with visible beat, threatened squares, elapsed-only timer and a move-preview risk named. specific 8: per-board counts and stories, palette, a queen climax. correct 8: clean English. 'Gambit' is used loosely. overall 8.

judge.why: X gives the builder metre coordinates and one consistent hazard plan with a respectful ending. Y has nice cultural touches but contradicts itself on where the hazards go and spends the whole session as timer.
judge.reason_on: fit: a 150 s race inside a 3-min slot leaves room for the intro; respects the temple (no Buddha images or monks as props) and ends on a calm รดน้ำขอพร, which suits tourists and families. buildable: 6 checkpoints, 3 hazards and a portal, with spawn, CPs, hazards and trees laid out in real metres and in order. safe: a dry play area kept apart from real splashing, the trees treated as hard exclusion zones, a 1.2 m corridor; but spectator_view says players 'วิ่งเข้าเส้นชัย' (run to the finish). specific: exact coordinates, red reserved for hazards, a south-side climax. correct: the test question misspells 'นักท่องเที่ยง'; the cultural content is accurate. overall: ready to hand over.
judge.reason_off: fit: the race format is right, but 'two lanes' means little when each racer walks their own copy, and timeLimit 180 uses the whole 3-min session with no room for the intro. buildable: the layout puts the climax hazards at (0.66,0.58) 'before the flower-flag checkpoint', but CP5 is at (0.78,0.38) and the flow places them after it, so the docs contradict each other. safe: an explicit no-running rule, dark-red white-rimmed hazards for noon glare, nothing attached to the trees. specific: normalised coordinates only, and the hazard count is loose. correct: the sand-pagoda (ก่อเจดีย์ทราย) and jasmine customs are accurate and respectful; 'ส่งพรน้ำเย็น' is awkward, and 'เชียร์ชื่อทีม' refers to teams that don't exist. overall: good but needs tidying.

judge.why: X is more concrete (metre coordinates, tree exclusions) and catches the real Songkran hazard of water on headsets. Y's lanes and timing don't hold together.
judge.reason_on: fit 7: sacred figures are kept out of play, it closes on a calm รดน้ำขอพร beat, and the 150 s limit fits a 3-minute slot with intro. Like Y, it never considers that foreign tourists may not read the Thai-only labels. buildable 8: 6 checkpoints, 3 hazards and 2 tree exclusion zones, all given in metres and consistent with the sketch. safe_mr 8: it alone flags that Songkran water splashes and wet floors threaten the non-waterproof headsets and requires a dry, isolated area, and it warns about 4 bodies crowding. But spectator_view says players 'วิ่งเข้าเส้นชัย'. specific 9: full coordinates, a noon palette, the climax placed toward the south spectators. correct 7: an odd 'ริมคลองสงกรานต์' label and 'นักท่องเที่ยง' typo. overall 8.
judge.reason_off: fit 6: a respectful theme, but Thai-only labels for foreign tourists, and timeLimit 180 eats the whole 3-minute session with no room for the intro. buildable 7: normalized coordinates are given, but 'two lanes' means nothing when every racer has an identical copy, and the sketch omits most checkpoints. safe_mr 6: walk-only and dark-red, white-rimmed hazards for noon glare, but no word about real splash water or the shared floor beyond 'ระวังผู้เล่นรอบตัว'. specific 7: hex palette and hero pieces. correct 8: jasmine and the sand-chedi (ก่อเจดีย์ทราย) tradition are accurate and nicely chosen. overall 6.

judge.why: Y states plainly that its hazards and zombies are static and sizes everything for the tiny room. X's story beats depend on closing rings and approaching zombies the runner cannot make.
judge.reason_on: fit: it reframes shooting as dodging zombie hands, with a short 2:20 run plus replay inside 5 min, which suits an experienced solo adult. buildable: two explicitly stationary hazards of about 0.35 m radius, 'no moving pursuing zombies', 4 CPs 0.5-1 m apart, 8-20 small props, all within the engine. safe: a walk-only rule, detours away from the bed, a 0.6 m spawn circle; like X, it doesn't face the fact that a 1.2 m corridor plus 0.6 m edges hardly fits a 2.2 m room with a bed. specific: radii, spacing, prop counts and a palette. correct: 'เริ่มภารกิจชุบชีวิต' / 'จุดชุบชีวิต' (resurrection) is an odd word for an evacuation. overall: buildable and honest.
judge.reason_off: fit: it says honestly that there is no shooting and uses a runner for a room under 3x3 m, but stretching a loop of 4 checkpoints in a 2.2 x 2.5 m room to 4:35 is padding. buildable: the key art's 'ring closing at the player's feet', 'hazards appear continuously' and 'zombies come closer' imply dynamic hazards and enemies the runner lacks; the option says 'ไม่มีคะแนนแข่ง' but then scores. safe: keeps the bed and jump scares out, but gives no clearance numbers for such a tight room. specific: positions are vague ('near the left-hand stop') and no sizes are given. correct: the theme has the typo 'ห้องพักรก'. overall: the motion it promises won't be built.

judge.why: Y sizes everything for a tiny bedroom and keeps hazards static and honest. X pads the timing and implies hazard behaviour the engine lacks.
judge.reason_on: fit 7: dodging zombie hands to reach a vaccine is a clear stand-in for shooting, and a realistic ~2:20 run with replays to cut time fits a regular VR player's 5 minutes. buildable 8: exactly 2 static hazards of ~0.35 m radius, checkpoints 0.5-1 m apart, 8-20 small props, and it says plainly that zombies don't move. safe_mr 7: walk-only rules, detours always away from the bed, no pursuers, though nobody reconciles the 1.2 m corridor with a room this small. specific 8: concrete radii, spacing, prop counts and hex palette. correct 7: 'จุดชุบชีวิต' / 'ภารกิจชุบชีวิต' (resurrection) is the wrong word for a rescue point. overall 7.
judge.reason_off: fit 6: it honestly says there is no shooting and that the room is under 3x3, and it uses 4 checkpoints. But stretching 4 checkpoints a metre apart across a 4:35 flow is padded, and a regular VR player will finish in a minute. buildable 6: the key art promises a red ring 'closing at the player's feet', which is dynamic behaviour the static runner hazards don't have. safe_mr 6: it asks whether the player backs toward the bed and avoids jump scares, but gives no sizes or distances for a 2.2x2.5 m floor. specific 6: two hazards, a palette, labels. correct 6: the theme line has a garbled word ('ห้องพักรก'). overall 6.

judge.why: Both are strong. X is a little more tuned to frail first-timers (no score in play, chest-height signs, staff and chair placement) and avoids floor art that looks like water.
judge.reason_on: fit: a 5-stop morning-market loop with no hazards and no timer, ending beside the friends' seats for sharing memories; it fits submission and narrative for 60-75 first-timers. buildable: plain checkpoints and a portal; 'ฟังเสียงวิทยุเก่า' leans on audio, and hiding the score is assumed rather than given. safe: staff beside spawn outside the route, rest chairs outside, chest-height cream-on-dark signs, no void, stops 2-3 m apart. specific: stop labels, sign contrast, staff and seating plan. correct: natural Thai, a respectful nostalgic setting. overall: ready to hand over.
judge.reason_off: fit: equally gentle and nostalgic (Thai dessert stall, canal bridge), but the HUD shows a running score, which slightly cuts against 'no rush'. buildable: 5 ordered CPs placed by compass direction, no hazards, timeLimit null. safe: names dizziness from looping and allows pauses at every stop; but a 'visual-only bridge beside a canal' on the floor may make unsteady seniors hesitate to step. specific: the palette, the clockwise layout and the friends on both sides are clear. correct: accurate, warm content. overall: good, a touch less tuned to frail players.

judge.why: Both are good. X is more tuned to frail first-timers: no visible score, staff and rest-chair placement, balance-focused tests and a seated fallback.
judge.reason_on: fit 9: a 5-stop slow loop with no timer and no hazards, ending near seated friends, with staff beside spawn and rest chairs outside the route. buildable 8: 5 checkpoints and timeLimit null are fine, but 'ทักทายพ่อค้า' hints at NPC talk and hiding the score from the HUD is assumed. safe_mr 9: never a void, signs at chest height, a PC fallback for unsteady walkers, and test questions that watch for wall-reaching and balance. specific 8: an old-radio quiet climax, cream-on-dark-wood signs, a 2-3 m spacing figure. correct 8. overall 8.
judge.reason_off: fit 8: a 5-stop market loop (coffee, produce, Thai desserts, canal bridge) that honours friends seated on both sides. buildable 8: a clean checkpoint and portal plan with clockwise compass placement. safe_mr 8: it flags dizziness from circling in a small room and lets the player rest at every stop, but the HUD shows score and the time bonus, which adds quiet pressure against 'ไม่ต้องรีบ'. specific 8: a 6-colour palette and named hero vignettes. correct 8: warm and accurate Thai market content, though the first 'risk' isn't really a risk. overall 8.

judge.why: Y is more concrete and more careful about six bodies on one court (separate spawns, pacing pause, hazard plan for each segment). X's copy still sells running and leaves hazard placement vague. Y's abyss bridge is its one safety concern.
judge.reason_on: fit: 9 CPs across the full 22 m with a hazard-free pause at CP7 and a climax by the families' long side, a good shape for challenge plus fellowship. buildable: 9 CPs is within 4-10, with hazard groups and spacing (2.5-9 m) defined per segment, all runner features; 'two lanes, own lane' for 6 players is muddled. safe: separate spawns, doors kept clear, explicit no-run and no-lane-cutting rules, and it names the shared-floor risk; but a race over a deep 'energy abyss' on a narrow-looking bridge invites vertigo. specific: per-segment hazard density, hero pieces, palette, door handling. correct: fine. overall: the stronger build doc, though the abyss should be softened.
judge.reason_off: fit: a 6-player neon race with a live leaderboard and wall screen for the families; but the pitch says 'เดิน-วิ่งพอประมาณ' and 'พุ่งเข้าโพรทัล', which goes against MR no-running. buildable: 7 CPs, hazards and a portal are fine, but hazard counts are vague ('portions of the final lane'). safe: it never addresses 6 people walking the same physical route at once beyond 'wide paths', and the climax copy urges speed. specific: CP labels and palette are fine; placement, spacing and hazard numbers are loose. correct: no errors. overall: workable but thin.

judge.why: Y has a real difficulty curve and climax staging, and it admits the six-bodies-on-one-floor problem. X invites running and its sketch contradicts its spectator plan.
judge.reason_on: fit 8: 9 checkpoints over the full 22 m, with the climax and portal set toward the family side and the wall leaderboard. buildable 7: per-player 'own lane and spawn' is not something the race engine does (every copy is identical), and the 'energy abyss' edges toward a void look. safe_mr 6: it at least names the shared-floor risk, separates 6 spawns, bans cutting lanes and running, and keeps the 4 doors clear, but a 'narrow bridge over abyss' in a race is a comfort risk. specific 8: a 1-2 teach, 4-6 dense, 7 rest, 8-9 climax pacing curve, 2.5-9 m spacing, exact labels. correct 7: the title 'ศูนย์วิกฤต' reads like a crisis hotline. overall 7.
judge.reason_off: fit 7: 7 checkpoints, 300 s, 6-player live leaderboard and neon all match the brief. buildable 7: only engine parts, but it says 'two lanes' and also 'not two intersecting courses', which leaves the lanes undefined. safe_mr 5: the pitch says 'เดิน-วิ่งพอประมาณ' and 'พุ่งเข้าโพรทัล', which invites running, and it never deals with 6 bodies walking the same physical route. specific 6: it has a palette and labels, but the sketch puts the spectators at x=0.04 while the dodge and portal sit mid-court, which contradicts the plan to stage key moments toward them. correct 7: no errors, but the copy is generic. overall 6.
